title: Arrow kernels and cokernels preserve exact colimits
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $J$ a category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose colimits of shape $J$ exist in $\mathcal M$ and the colimit functor $\mathcal M^J\to\mathcal M$ preserves finite limits. Then the functors $\ker,\operatorname{coker}:\operatorname{Arrow}(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M$ preserve colimits of shape $J$. In particular they carry every colimit cocone of arrows to the canonical colimit cocone on the kernels and cokernels.

source.place: Final paragraph: filtered colimits are exact, hence commute with kernels and cokernels.

proof.text: A diagram of arrows is a natural transformation of its vertex diagrams. Pointwise kernels and cokernels are kernels and cokernels in the functor category, by the pointwise universal properties. Applying the exact colimit functor preserves the kernel; applying the colimit functor preserves the cokernel because colimits commute with colimits. Identify the vertex colimits with the vertices of the given colimit arrow. Uniqueness in the kernel/cokernel universal properties identifies the induced maps with the canonical legs. This proves preservation of the specified cocones, not merely existence of abstract object isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: Final paragraph; expanded pointwise universal-property calculation.
